# gh-1655: [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).
- [ ] AC4: live check against `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7`: thinking without doubled punctuation; a tool-call turn executes each command exactly once.

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Pinned release must carry signed provenance
        run: bash scripts/check_install_pin.sh

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \

  # Aggregate required check: branch protection requires ONE stable context.
  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #280: PR-level BUILD verification. The gates above analyze and
  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,
  # web-only compile errors, asset manifest breakage), discovered later by
  # build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml at release time. Four parallel debug
  # legs below close that gap, gated on app/shared changes only (docs/core
  # PRs never pay). Debug mode on PRs: compile-truth is the goal; release-
  # only concerns (tree-shaking, R8, codesign) live in the nightly release
  # matrix (nightly.yml). Budgets (#177): ≤8 min warm / ≤15 min cold per
  # leg, ≤10 min wall added to an app-touching PR (legs run in parallel).
  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and
  # PR code never lands on the self-hosted release pool).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The
      # action's cache key embeds the resolved SDK version, so an SDK bump
      # in a PR never restores a poisoned cache (E1).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build web
        # E3: warnings (including the Wasm dry-run diagnostics) are allowed;
        # compile errors fail via the exit code — same fatal semantics as
        # the flutter-tests leg's analyze step.
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build web

  build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1

          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",

                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. ## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

# gh-1655: [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).
- [ ] AC4: live check against `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7`: thinking without doubled punctuation; a tool-call turn executes each command exactly once.

  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,
  # web-only compile errors, asset manifest breakage), discovered later by
  # build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml at release time. Four parallel debug
  # legs below close that gap, gated on app/shared changes only (docs/core
  # PRs never pay). Debug mode on PRs: compile-truth is the goal; release-
  # only concerns (tree-shaking, R8, codesign) live in the nightly release
  # matrix (nightly.yml). Budgets (#177): ≤8 min warm / ≤15 min cold per
  # leg, ≤10 min wall added to an app-touching PR (legs run in parallel).
  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and
  # PR code never lands on the self-hosted release pool).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The
      # action's cache key embeds the resolved SDK version, so an SDK bump
      # in a PR never restores a poisoned cache (E1).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build web
        # E3: warnings (including the Wasm dry-run diagnostics) are allowed;
        # compile errors fail via the exit code — same fatal semantics as
        # the flutter-tests leg's analyze step.
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build web

        run: |

          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

# gh-1655: [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).

  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #280: PR-level BUILD verification. The gates above analyze and
  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,
  # web-only compile errors, asset manifest breakage), discovered later by
  # build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml at release time. Four parallel debug
  # legs below close that gap, gated on app/shared changes only (docs/core
  # PRs never pay). Debug mode on PRs: compile-truth is the goal; release-
  # only concerns (tree-shaking, R8, codesign) live in the nightly release
  # matrix (nightly.yml). Budgets (#177): ≤8 min warm / ≤15 min cold per
  # leg, ≤10 min wall added to an app-touching PR (legs run in parallel).
  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and
  # PR code never lands on the self-hosted release pool).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The
      # action's cache key embeds the resolved SDK version, so an SDK bump
      # in a PR never restores a poisoned cache (E1).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build web
        # E3: warnings (including the Wasm dry-run diagnostics) are allowed;
        # compile errors fail via the exit code — same fatal semantics as
        # the flutter-tests leg's analyze step.
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build web

  build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. All output must be Markdown. ### Required files 1. `outputs/response.md` - Markdown fix summary for the top-level PR comm…

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

# gh-1655: [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).
- [ ] AC4: live check against `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7`: thinking without doubled punctuation; a tool-call turn executes each command exactly once.

  # Aggregate required check: branch protection requires ONE stable context.
  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #280: PR-level BUILD verification. The gates above analyze and
  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,
  # web-only compile errors, asset manifest breakage), discovered later by
  # build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml at release time. Four parallel debug
  # legs below close that gap, gated on app/shared changes only (docs/core
  # PRs never pay). Debug mode on PRs: compile-truth is the goal; release-
  # only concerns (tree-shaking, R8, codesign) live in the nightly release
  # matrix (nightly.yml). Budgets (#177): ≤8 min warm / ≤15 min cold per
  # leg, ≤10 min wall added to an app-touching PR (legs run in parallel).
  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and
  # PR code never lands on the self-hosted release pool).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The
      # action's cache key embeds the resolved SDK version, so an SDK bump
      # in a PR never restores a poisoned cache (E1).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build web
        # E3: warnings (including the Wasm dry-run diagnostics) are allowed;
        # compile errors fail via the exit code — same fatal semantics as
        # the flutter-tests leg's analyze step.
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build web

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients

      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal

      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json

        run: |

## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.

# gh-1655: [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

## Description

## [BUG] aiin/JoinGonka relay stutter: doubled punctuation in thinking + duplicated tool-call execution

### Product frame

OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka fronting MiniMax-M2.7, observed via provider `aiin`) stutter stream frames: punctuation-only reasoning tokens arrive twice, and a tool-call frame can be re-sent with a freshly generated `id`. The shared adapter must tolerate both — every relay downstream of `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits this.

### Evidence

Session of 2026-10-16 15:53 (owner clip, `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7`):

1. **Thinking text has every sentence-punctuation char doubled** — `The user said "Hello"" - a simple greeting.. I should respond in a friendly,, helpful way…`, `I'm Fa,,`, `today??`, `help::`. Letters, `I'm`, `&` are NEVER doubled — punctuation arrives as standalone deltas, and a 1-char overlap/stutter survives the dedupe.
2. **The same bash command executed twice in one turn** — records show `bash {"command":"js hello.js"}` twice, same `startedAt` to the millisecond, different callIds (`chatcmpl-tool-bd624c1dd04fbbc9` / `chatcmpl-tool-9b456367dc7027d2`), one returned clean output, the other `SyntaxError: redeclaration of 'name'` through a different eval path. The model then hallucinated a justification ("I used `qjs` instead") to reconcile the phantom second run — wasted execution plus a confusing ledger.

### Root causes — both in `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`

- **C1 (thinking doubling):** `_dedupeOverlap` — the overlap trim loop is `for (var k = maxK; k >= 2; k--)`. A stutter of exactly 1 char (the punctuation token re-sent) is below the floor and is appended verbatim. ≥2-char stutters are already cleaned (the "Продродололжжж" comment case).
- **C2 (duplicate tool call):** `_ensureToolCallBlock` matches existing blocks only by `streamIndex` / `id`. A re-sent call frame carrying a NEW relay-generated id and no (or another) `index` misses the lookup and spawns a second `ToolCallStreamingBlock` with identical name + arguments → both execute.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 fix:** trim 1-char overlaps too. Ellipsis guard: do NOT trim when the remaining delta starts with the same char again (legit `...` continuations); otherwise a leading single char equal to the current tail is an overlap. Keep the full-snapshot branch and the 64-char window as-is.
- **C2 fix:** in `_ensureToolCallBlock`, when lookup misses and the incoming frame has no usable identity match, check the LAST registered tool-call block of the current message: if its name is non-empty, equals the incoming name, and its `partialArgs` is empty or a prefix of the incoming arguments — treat the frame as a re-send (merge into the existing block, adopt the newer id only if the old one is empty) instead of spawning a block.
- **C3 — regression guards:** unit tests simulating a stuttering relay: (a) reasoning deltas `greeting`, `.`, `.`, ` I should` → thinking contains `greeting. I should`; (b) `...` ellipsis split across deltas survives untrimmed; (c) tool-call frames A(id1, name, args) then B(id2, same name, same args) → ONE block, args correct; (d) two genuinely different calls in one message still produce two blocks.
- **C4 — no behavior change for clean relays:** OpenRouter/DeepSeek/litellm-style clean delta streams must produce byte-identical output (existing adapter tests stay green).

### Test matrix

- `test/providers/openai_completions_dedupe_test.dart` (or the file where `_dedupeOverlap` is covered today): cases C3a–C3d.
- Existing openai-completions adapter tests: unchanged green (C4).

### Platform inventory

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart` only (shared adapter; `aiin`, openrouter, deepseek and every custom baseUrl route through it). No session/protocol/UI changes. Pure Dart, no new deps.

### Security

No new data flows; all parsing stays on already-received frames.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: stuttering-reasoning fixtures produce clean thinking text (C3a), ellipsis intact (C3b).
- [ ] AC2: re-sent tool-call frame with fresh id does not execute twice (C3c); distinct calls still distinct (C3d).
- [ ] AC3: existing adapter tests untouched and green (C4).

  # Skipped legs (path-filtered out) count as pass — a docs PR must go green
  # on static alone.

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #280: PR-level BUILD verification. The gates above analyze and
  # test but never COMPILE a platform target — a PR could go green while
  # breaking the iOS/macOS/Android/web build (pod/entitlement drift,
  # web-only compile errors, asset manifest breakage), discovered later by
  # build-mobile.yml/build-macos.yml at release time. Four parallel debug
  # legs below close that gap, gated on app/shared changes only (docs/core
  # PRs never pay). Debug mode on PRs: compile-truth is the goal; release-
  # only concerns (tree-shaking, R8, codesign) live in the nightly release
  # matrix (nightly.yml). Budgets (#177): ≤8 min warm / ≤15 min cold per
  # leg, ≤10 min wall added to an app-touching PR (legs run in parallel).
  # E4: both macOS legs use GitHub-hosted macos-latest — every job gets its
  # own ephemeral VM, so ios+macos are never serialized on one runner (and
  # PR code never lands on the self-hosted release pool).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  build-web:
    name: Build web (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Pinned to the same SDK as the release path (#281): 3.47.x. The
      # action's cache key embeds the resolved SDK version, so an SDK bump
      # in a PR never restores a poisoned cache (E1).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build web
        # E3: warnings (including the Wasm dry-run diagnostics) are allowed;
        # compile errors fail via the exit code — same fatal semantics as
        # the flutter-tests leg's analyze step.
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build web

  build-android:
    name: Build Android APK (debug)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The google-services Gradle plugin (applied unconditionally in
      # android/app/build.gradle.kts) refuses to run without this file.
      # #622 commits a placeholder carrying BOTH flavor clients
      # (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god); keep it whenever present — the
      # debug-APK smoke pins the store flavor (`--flavor store`, only the
      # dev.fa1.app client is needed); god compile truth is covered by the
      # flavor matrix release job. Only when the file is missing
      # (old forks/history) seed the structurally-valid dev.fa1.app
      # placeholder — debug APKs never talk to Firebase with it; the goal
      # here is compile truth (#280).
      - name: Create placeholder google-services.json
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f android/app/google-services.json ]; then
            echo "committed google-services.json present (dev.fa1.app + dev.fa1.app.god) — keeping it"
          else
            cat > android/app/google-services.json << 'EOF'
          {
            "project_info": {
              "project_number": "000000000000",
              "project_id": "fa1-placeholder",
              "storage_bucket": "fa1-placeholder.appspot.com"
            },
            "client": [
              {
                "client_info": {
                  "mobilesdk_app_id": "1:000000000000:android:0000000000000000000000",
                  "android_client_info": {
                    "package_name": "dev.fa1.app"
                  }
                },
                "oauth_client": [],
                "api_key": [
                  {
                    "current_key": "AIzaSyA-PLACEHOLDER-KEY-FOR-DEBUG-BUILDS-000000"
                  }
                ],
                "services": {
                  "appinvite_service": {
                    "other_platform_oauth_client": []
                  }
                }
              }
            ],
            "configuration_version": "1"
          }
          EOF
          fi

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache so the
      # build hook never downloads litertlm-android_arm64.tar.gz mid-build
      # — one release-asset CDN 500 red'd this leg and the aggregate
      # Quality gate. Same hardening as the macOS companion-dylibs step.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      - name: flutter build apk (debug)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter build apk --debug --flavor store

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS (debug, unsigned)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - ## PR Description

Closes #1655
### Root Cause

Stuttering OpenAI-compatible relays (JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7 via `aiin`) re-send stream frames; the shared adapter mishandled both shapes: `_dedupeOverlap` trimmed overlaps only for `k >= 2`, so a 1-char punctuation stutter survived (doubled punctuation in thinking), and `_ensureToolCallBlock` matched blocks only by `streamIndex`/`id`, so a re-sent call frame with a fresh id spawned a second identical block and executed the command twice.

### Fix

- `lib/src/providers/openai_completions.dart`:
  - `_dedupeOverlap`: trim 1-char overlaps too, with an ellipsis guard (a delta repeating its leading char is a legit `...` continuation, not a seam); full-snapshot branch and 64-char window unchanged.
  - `_ensureToolCallBlock` + new `_matchResentToolCallBlock`: on a lookup miss, a frame whose name equals the last registered block's name with `partialArgs` empty or a prefix of the incoming args is a re-send — merge into that block (newer id adopted only if the old is empty), appending only the non-overlapping argument suffix.

### Test Coverage

- `test/providers/openai_completions_test.dart`: stutter-trim (`greeting`, `.`, `.` → `greeting. I should`), ellipsis intact (`hmm`, `.`, `..` → `hmm...`), re-sent frame with fresh id → ONE block/one execution, distinct calls → two blocks. All failed-before/green-after as specified.
- Existing sliding-window fixture updated: `'Продолжжжжаем'` → `'Продолжжжаем'` (it baked in the surviving 1-char stutter); clean-delta cases byte-identical (C4).
- Full suite: 6549 passed, 19 failed — all 19 verified pre-existing on the clean base commit (`124f1e0`) via a detached worktree run (env-dependent PTY/CLI suites already red on main per gh-1649); provider suites: 827/827 green.

### Notes

- Merge fires only on an id/index lookup miss — clean relays are unaffected by construction.
- AC4 (live `aiin/JoinGonka/MiniMax-M2.7` check) is not executable in this environment; the fixtures reproduce both observed defects at the adapter level.
