blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

blocks.text:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK so Gradle configuration never
  triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download mid-build. gh-1655: one
  truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download ("Error on ZipFile unknown
  archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android leg — and the aggregate
  Quality gate with it — because AGP's in-configuration auto-install path
  has NO retry. The NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's
  own gradle plugin source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves
  to — no second pin to drift), the install is skipped when the NDK is
  already present, and the download itself is bounded-retried — the same
  hardening the flutter_gemma Android seed carries (gh-1468). Companion
  guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed; skip the download entirely.
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
          rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
            echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
          sleep 10
        done
        echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
        exit 1

blocks.text:
Their guard test is thorough (AC1-AC5, mirrors the gemma pattern faithfully). Now let me review the actual workflow wiring diffs for defects. Let me look at the exact diffs introduced by 09ff1bc08e for the three workflows.

One thing I noticed in the action: the retry loop checks sdkmanager exit code but does NOT verify source.properties AFTER a successful install (only the pre-check for idempotency). sdkmanager --install exits nonzero on corrupt archive (that's how the leg failed), so exit-code-checking is defensible. Their guard AC1 doesn't require verification either. It's a minor gap, not a defect per se. Hmm — should I add a post-install `Pkg.Revision` verification? It'd be a small patch to their action + one guard assertion. Risk: `Pkg.Revision` format — for NDK 28.2.13676358 the source.properties does contain `Pkg.Revision=28.2.13676358`. Let me verify that claim... I can't download the NDK here quickly (huge). Actually — the format: NDK source.properties has `Pkg.Revision=28.2.13676358`? For r26b it's `Pkg.Revision=26.1.109125`. Yes, Pkg.Revision is the exact version triple for NDK packages.

But hold on — being surgical matters more. Their implementation exits 0 only when sdkmanager --install succeeds. If sdkmanager succeeded but left a partial tree (rare), gradle would fail loudly with a clear error. The verification adds marginal value. Their guard test explicitly documents the discipline they chose. Adding my `Pkg.Revision` check would improve robustness... but it risks a FALSE failure: sdkmanager installs `source.properties` with `Pkg.Revision=28.2.13676358`? Let me double check: for NDK r28c, dir `28.2.13676358`... The source.properties inside contains:
```
Pkg.Desc = Android NDK
Pkg.Revision = 28.2.13676358
```
Hmm — is it `Pkg.Revision = 28.2.13676358` (with spaces) or `Pkg.Revision=28.2.13676358`? NDK source.properties historically uses `Pkg.Revision = 26.1.109125`? Let me check an actual NDK source.properties format... From android-ndk-r26d: 
```
Pkg.Desc = Android NDK
Pkg.Revision = 26.3.11579264
Pkg.Revision = ...
```
Actually I recall NDK's source.properties:
```
Pkg.Desc = Android NDK
Pkg.Revision = 25.2.9519653
```
The sdkmanager package.properties uses spaces around `=`. Platform properties files (java.util.Properties format) allow both. If I grep with `^Pkg.Revision=28...$` it could false-negative against `Pkg.Revision = 28...`. That's exactly the kind of fragile verification that turns a green leg red. Given their exit-code approach + the pre-existing failure mode produces nonzero exit anyway, their implementation is adequate. Don't patch — review verdict: sound.

Now check the wiring diffs for the three workflows. Also verify no OTHER modifications are pending in the tree (git status was clean except my now-deleted files). Let me view the diff of 09ff1bc08e for workflows, then validate the YAML files parse, and check for any other uncommitted state. Also confirm the branch is clean of my duplicates now.

Their guard test is faithful to the gemma doctrine and thorough (AC1–AC5). Reviewing their action: exit-code-based retry with `rm -rf` before each attempt, runtime version resolution, idempotent skip — sound. Found the exact bug:

```
test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart 279:14  main.<fn>.<fn>
```

Line 279 in the CURRENT (f47f6e3fd3) guard test is:
```dart
        ...Directory('/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter')
            .listSync()
```

On the CI test-core runner, `/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter` doesn't EXIST (this dev runner happens to have it; the test-core runner doesn't), and `Directory.listSync()` on a nonexistent dir throws `PathNotFoundException` — the test crashed instead of skipping. Classic: should guard with `.existsSync()`.

And the second failing leg, `Hostile ambient env` — probably runs the same test file under hostile env and crashed the same way. Let me verify quickly, then fix.

Fix (TDD): the failing scenario is "no /opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter dir" → must print the named skip instead of crashing. RED: I can reproduce locally by pointing the candidates check at a nonexistent dir — but the path is hardcoded. Simplest reproduction: temporarily rename... can't rename /opt paths here (root?). Actually I CAN test the unit: extract resolution into a helper that takes a dir and use `.existsSync()` guard. But per TDD rules, write a test that reproduces: a test asserting the guard test's own resolution helper handles a missing directory... The guard test file is itself the test. Minimal correct fix: add `.existsSync()` check. To honor RED-GREEN: I can demonstrate the crash locally with `FLUTTER_ROOT` unset and the hostedtoolcache path missing — can't easily simulate the hardcoded path. 

Alternative honest approach: make the resolution robust AND testable:
```dart
final hostedCache = Directory('/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter');
final candidates = <String>[
  if (envRoot != null && envRoot.isNotEmpty) envRoot,
  ...?(!hostedCache.existsSync() ? null : hostedCache.listSync()...),
];
```
Even better: also try `command -v flutter`-style resolution (which is what MY version did — resolve the binary then take parent.parent, with try/catch on IOException). The PathNotFoundException is a FileSystemException subclass... my version caught `IOException` — PathNotFoundException extends FileSystemException extends IOException. My resolveFlutterSdkRoot had `on IOException { return null; }` around listSync-free logic (I used `which`) — that's why mine wouldn't crash. But mine is deleted; converging on their file, I just need to fix THEIR line 279 area with an existsSync guard.

For RED: add a unit-testable seam? Overkill. The pragmatic TDD-compliant move: the crash IS the reproduction (CI log). The fix: existsSync guard. Verification: run the guard test locally in an env where the candidates dir is absent — I can simulate by running with a modified HOME? No, path hardcoded. I could run with `FLUTTER_ROOT` pointing to the real SDK (envRoot branch short-circuits first, so hostedtoolcache listSync never runs → can't reproduce the crash locally with my env). 

Hmm — to truly verify the fix handles the CI case, I can write a tiny throwaway dart snippet replicating the FIXED expression against a nonexistent dir and confirm no throw + named skip. Plus run the full guard test file locally (both branches: with FLUTTER_ROOT set and with FLUTTER_ROOT unset but hostedtoolcache present — exercising the hostedtoolcache branch end-to-end, since on my box the dir exists).

Also `Hostile ambient env` leg — check what it failed on. Let me grep its log. If it's the same crash, one fix covers both.

Additionally, their `candidates.first` — if envRoot is set AND exists, but the gradle file moved → named skip. OK.

Now — wait, there's a deeper question. Should AC5 even RUN the hostedtoolcache branch on test-core CI runners where flutter isn't provisioned? The named-skip handles it: no candidates → skip line. Good.

Found the exact bug:

```
test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart 279:14  main.<fn>.<fn>
```

Line 279 in the CURRENT (f47f6e3fd3) guard test is:
```dart
        ...Directory('/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter')
            .listSync()
```

On the CI test-core runner, `/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter` doesn't EXIST (this dev runner happens to have it; the test-core runner doesn't), and `Directory.listSync()` on a nonexistent dir throws `PathNotFoundException` — the test crashed instead of skipping. Classic: should guard with `.existsSync()`.

And the second failing leg, `Hostile ambient env` — probably runs the same test file under hostile env and crashed the same way. Let me verify quickly, then fix.

Fix (TDD): the failing scenario is "no /opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter dir" → must print the named skip instead of crashing. RED: I can reproduce locally by pointing the candidates check at a nonexistent dir — but the path is hardcoded. Simplest reproduction: temporarily rename... can't rename /opt paths here (root?). Actually I CAN test the unit: extract resolution into a helper that takes a dir and use `.existsSync()` guard. But per TDD rules, write a test that reproduces: a test asserting the guard test's own resolution helper handles a missing directory... The guard test file is itself the test. Minimal correct fix: add `.existsSync()` check. To honor RED-GREEN: I can demonstrate the crash locally with `FLUTTER_ROOT` unset and the hostedtoolcache path missing — can't easily simulate the hardcoded path. 

Alternative honest approach: make the resolution robust AND testable:
```dart
final hostedCache = Directory('/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter');
final candidates = <String>[
  if (envRoot != null && envRoot.isNotEmpty) envRoot,
  ...?(!hostedCache.existsSync() ? null : hostedCache.listSync()...),
];
```
Even better: also try `command -v flutter`-style resolution (which is what MY version did — resolve the binary then take parent.parent, with try/catch on IOException). The PathNotFoundException is a FileSystemException subclass... my version caught `IOException` — PathNotFoundException extends FileSystemException extends IOException. My resolveFlutterSdkRoot had `on IOException { return null; }` around listSync-free logic (I used `which`) — that's why mine wouldn't crash. But mine is deleted; converging on their file, I just need to fix THEIR line 279 area with an existsSync guard.

For RED: add a unit-testable seam? Overkill. The pragmatic TDD-compliant move: the crash IS the reproduction (CI log). The fix: existsSync guard. Verification: run the guard test locally in an env where the candidates dir is absent — I can simulate by running with a modified HOME? No, path hardcoded. I could run with `FLUTTER_ROOT` pointing to the real SDK (envRoot branch short-circuits first, so hostedtoolcache listSync never runs → can't reproduce the crash locally with my env). 

Hmm — to truly verify the fix handles the CI case, I can write a tiny throwaway dart snippet replicating the FIXED expression against a nonexistent dir and confirm no throw + named skip. Plus run the full guard test file locally (both branches: with FLUTTER_ROOT set and with FLUTTER_ROOT unset but hostedtoolcache present — exercising the hostedtoolcache branch end-to-end, since on my box the dir exists).

Also `Hostile ambient env` leg — check what it failed on. Let me grep its log. If it's the same crash, one fix covers both.

Additionally, their `candidates.first` — if envRoot is set AND exists, but the gradle file moved → named skip. OK.

Now — wait, there's a deeper question. Should AC5 even RUN the hostedtoolcache branch on test-core CI runners where flutter isn't provisioned? The named-skip handles it: no candidates → skip line. Good.

Classic: should guard with `.existsSync()`.

And the second failing leg, `Hostile ambient env` — probably runs the same test file under hostile env and crashed the same way. Let me verify quickly, then fix.

```dart
final hostedCache = Directory('/opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter');
final candidates = <String>[

  ...?(!hostedCache.existsSync() ? null : hostedCache.listSync()...),
];
```

The PathNotFoundException is a FileSystemException subclass... my version caught `IOException` — PathNotFoundException extends FileSystemException extends IOException. My resolveFlutterSdkRoot had `on IOException { return null; }` around listSync-free logic (I used `which`) — that's why mine wouldn't crash. But mine is deleted; converging on their file, I just need to fix THEIR line 279 area with an existsSync guard.

+/// SDK roots to probe for the gradle plugin source, most-specific first:
+/// FLUTTER_ROOT, then any hostedtoolcache Flutter install carrying a
+/// bin/flutter. [hostedCache] is probed only when it exists — the CI
+/// test-core runners carry no /opt/hostedtoolcache/flutter at all, and an
+/// unguarded listSync there crashed AC5 with PathNotFoundException
+/// instead of degrading to the named skip (gh-1655 rework: both
+/// `Core tests shard 1/4` and `Hostile ambient env` red on 2026-10-17).
+List<String> flutterSdkCandidates(Directory? hostedCache) {
+  final envRoot = Platform.environment['FLUTTER_ROOT'];
+  return [
+    if (envRoot != null && envRoot.isNotEmpty) envRoot,
+    if (hostedCache != null && hostedCache.existsSync())
+      ...hostedCache
+          .listSync()
+          .whereType<Directory>()
+          .map((d) => d.path)
+          .where((p) => File('$p/flutter/bin/flutter').existsSync()),
+  ];
+}","path":"test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart"}

- name: SM merge guard self-test (gh-1568)
        run: bash scripts/sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh

      # gh-1625: the release-event dedupe pre-check is fixture-self-tested
      # against a PATH-stubbed gh — recent/stale/no push run for the tag,
      # the 6h window boundary, non-release arms making NO API call, and
      # a failing `gh run list` degrading to dedupe=false — so the
      # release twin's short-circuit cannot rot silently before the next
      # release (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Release dedupe self-test (gh-1625)
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh

      # #1431: the size-budget gate's own red exits are fixture-tested
      # (#1100 pattern) — an engine rev-hash rename must UPDATE not NEW,
      # vendored engine churn warns instead of reddening, first-party
      # payload still fails hard, and the 20+hex regex leaves first-party
      # paths that merely contain hex alone.
      - name: Size manifest gate self-test (#1431)
        run: python3 scripts/test_size_manifest.py

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
